# Code of Conduct

## The short version

Be decent to people. Assume the person you're replying to is acting in good
faith until they give you a concrete reason to think otherwise.

## What's expected

- Keep criticism on the work, not the person who did it.
- Accept that other people have different levels of experience, different
  first languages, and different amounts of time to spend here.
- When you disagree, say what you'd do instead.

## What isn't acceptable

Harassment of any kind, personal or political attacks, publishing anyone's
private information, and deliberately derailing discussions. This applies in
issues, pull requests, commit messages, and anywhere else the project is
discussed.

## Scope

This applies to everyone taking part, maintainers included, in any project
space and when representing the project elsewhere.

## Reporting

Report a problem through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on this
repository, or by contacting the maintainer directly. Reports are handled
privately. The maintainer may edit or delete contributions, and block accounts,
where this document isn't being respected.

## Reference

This is a short original text, not a fork of a standard code of conduct. If you
want a fuller framework, the
[Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org) is the usual
starting point.
